newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan caretakers strive to rebuild f/x reserves.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan caretakers strive to rebuild f/x reserves.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker government still hopes to rebuild foreign reserves to $1 billion by the end of its three-month term, its finance chief said on Wednesday.
"We might or might not be able to reach that figure," Shahid Javed Burki, the prime minister's finance and economic affairs adviser, told a news conference in Islamabad.
President Farooq Leghari appointed the caretaker government after sacking Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5 due to disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Burki was speaking as the Supreme Court threw out Bhutto's legal challenge to Leghari's action, clearing the way for Monday's national and provincial elections to go ahead.

Central bank data show foreign exchange reserves, excluding gold and Special Drawing Rights, fell to $689 million on January 23 from $785 million a week earlier and $1.663 billion on January 25, 1996.
"Today, reserves are closer to $800 million," Burki said, adding that Pakistan had just received an $80 million tranche of a standby loan from the International Monetary Fund.

"We have paid most of the bills due in January. The problem has been that it is not easy for Pakistan to raise resources. We were very badly hurt by Moody's downgrade," he said, referring the U.S. rating agency's decision on November 8 to cut Pakistan's sovereign ceiling foreign-currency debt to B2 from B1.
He said he hoped the release of the latest tranche of the IMF standby loan would improve Pakistan's access to funds.
The IMF agreed in December to resume disbursements of a stalled $600 million standby facility and expand it by $231 million and released an $80 million tranche at that time.
The IMF insists that Pakistan cut its 1996/97 (July-June) budget deficit to four percent of gross domestic product from 6.3 percent in 1995/96.
Burki said any new elected government should make an all-out effort to meet the deficit target. "Please take the four percent target very seriously," he urged his successor.
